option_relations.rationale: Optic nerve astrocytoma is a type of optic nerve glioma, which is part of the broader diagnosis of malignant optic nerve glioma (IDH-mutant astrocytoma, WHO grade 3/4) with vitreous seeding and secondary central retinal artery and vein occlusion.

Primary optic nerve glioma is a type of optic nerve glioma, which is part of the broader diagnosis of malignant optic nerve glioma (IDH-mutant astrocytoma, WHO grade 3/4) with vitreous seeding and secondary central retinal artery and vein occlusion.

Optic nerve glioma (astrocytoma) is a type of optic nerve glioma, which is part of the broader diagnosis of malignant optic nerve glioma (IDH-mutant astrocytoma, WHO grade 3/4) with vitreous seeding and secondary central retinal artery and vein occlusion.

Glioblastoma (WHO grade IV) is a distinct entity from the malignant optic nerve glioma (IDH-mutant astrocytoma, WHO grade 3/4) described in the leaf, even with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension. The biopsy findings point to an astrocytic neoplasm with specific markers (IDH-1 mutant, ATRX loss) that align with the leaf's more specific diagnosis rather than a general glioblastoma.
